Definition: second person singular imperative active of G1492; used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!:--behold, lo, see.
BiblicalUsage: Behold is a word that stops you and points, and John the Baptist uses it at the moment that matters most. In John 1:29 he sees Jesus coming and says, Behold the Lamb of God, in John 1:36 he says it again the next day, and in John 11:3 the sisters send word to Jesus, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe behold is the right word for those moments: stop, look, and see who is standing in front of you.
RelatedEvents: The Baptism of Jesus; Raising of Lazarus; The Calling of the First Disciples
